findings.where: Desktop, the whole content column: the intro, Surf, Vibe and What to look for text against the Good for chip rows and the coming-soon notice
findings.fault: The text sits in a narrow column, about 520 px, pinned to the left of a container about 1050 px wide. The right half of every text section is empty sand. The chip rows then run to about 1155 px and the notice box runs the full 1050 px, so the page has three different right edges. Inside the full-width notice the text still stops at the narrow column's width, which leaves the right half of the box as empty red. Continuity fails: the eye finds no shared right edge, so the empty space looks like an unfinished layout, not a planned measure.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker opening the guide on a laptop to plan the next hop. The first screen looks lopsided and half-empty, as if the page failed to load a sidebar or image, and that undercuts the 'effortless', crafted feel the brand promises.

findings.where: Bottom of the page, the 'MantaHostels is launching…' notice compared with the h1 and the guide sections
findings.fault: Squint test: the notice is a heavy, saturated, full-width block, and it wins the page outright over the h1 and every guide section. It is an aside about Manta's own state, yet it is the strongest figure on the page and outweighs the Canggu content the page exists to deliver. Figure and ground are inverted: the aside is the figure and the guide is the ground.
findings.who_objects: A visitor skimming to judge whether Canggu suits them. Their eye is pulled to a block that tells them nothing about Canggu and reads like an alert, so the guide content feels secondary and the page's main message seems to be 'not ready'.

findings.where: Section headings: 'Surf', 'Vibe', 'Good for', 'WHAT TO LOOK FOR' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Four sibling sections have four different heading treatments. 'Surf' and 'Good for' are plain ink headings. 'Vibe' is italic, teal and underlined. 'What to look for' is a small, tracked, uppercase label. Similarity is broken, so the sections don't read as peers. 'What to look for' reads as a minor caption under the chips rather than its own section, even though it holds the page's most practical advice. 'Vibe' reads as a link, not a heading.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker scanning on a phone for what to check in a hostel. The section that answers that question is the least prominent heading on the page, so it is easy to skip. The odd 'Vibe' heading looks like a tappable link that does nothing.

findings.where: 'Good for' chip group: worst on phone, where it wraps to five ragged rows; also desktop
findings.fault: Twelve chips use six or more fill colours and a different contrasting border colour each. The colours vary with no meaning, so similarity groups the chips by arbitrary colour instead of reading as one list. This is the busiest section on the page, and on phone it becomes a ragged multicoloured block of five rows that outweighs the text sections around it.
findings.who_objects: A visitor checking whether Canggu fits them ('am I a surfer, remote worker, solo traveller?'). The colour noise slows scanning a simple list of traits and suggests the colours mean categories when they don't.

findings.fault: The links wrap after 'How we rank', so a '·' separator dangles at the end of the first line and 'Report content' starts the second line with no separator. The line reads as broken.
findings.who_objects: Few would notice. A careful visitor looking for the contact or report link sees a small rendering slip in the footer.
